description: We are a team interested in agriculture, geospatial technology, remote sensing, and satellite data. Our team has experience with GIS, UAV imagery, weather data, agriculture, data analysis, and software development. For the "Dancing with SARs" challenge, we want to explore how SAR data can help us understand changes on Earth. We want to combine SAR with other data to create a practical solution for a real-world problem
summary:
LAND MEMORY is a web dashboard that shows how different patches of land respond to rain, using NASA's NISAR radar. We tested it in Haiti's Artibonite valley, where both floods and dry spells threaten farming.

For each 250 m square, we pair NISAR HH and HV radar echoes from June to October 2026 with NASA GPM IMERG rainfall, and fit a simple rule: how much the echo changes when it has rained recently. A square is flagged when its latest echo differs from its own history, or when its response differs from similar land nearby. On the latest pass, 5.3% of 13,860 squares were flagged. We treat those as places to inspect, not as confirmed change.

A Scenario Explorer lets users test "what if it rains 50 mm?" with a simple statistical model. Radar echoes are not a direct measure of flooding or soil moisture, so LAND MEMORY points to where to look closer, not why.
details:
LAND MEMORY learns how each small square of land normally responds to rainfall, and flags squares that stop behaving as expected.

Live website: https://landmemory.pythonanywhere.com

Code: https://github.com/Lemayzeur/land_memory

Video: https://vimeo.com/1247139551

What it does

We built an interactive dashboard around NASA NISAR radar. Users click a square on the map, see its rain and radar history, see how it normally responds to rain, and check whether it behaves differently from its own past or from similar land nearby. It works anywhere NISAR data exists. Our demo area is the Artibonite valley in Haiti.

How it works

1. Radar: NISAR Level 2 GCOV data (provisional and validated), HH and HV channels, 11 passes on one track between June and October 2026, averaged to 250 m squares.

2. Rain: NASA GPM IMERG V07 Late daily rainfall, turned into an Antecedent Precipitation Index (API). The index gives recent rain more weight and keeps a fading memory of earlier days. Days with missing rain data are excluded, never counted as zero.

3. Learning: for each square and each polarization, we fit radar (dB) = a + b x API, and keep the slope, its uncertainty, and R-squared.

4. Two checks:

(A) hide one pass, predict it from the other passes, and compare it with what the satellite saw.

(B) compare the square's slope with similar land cover from ESA WorldCover.

5. Scenario Explorer: users choose rainfall (0 to 150 mm), previous wetness, dry days afterwards, and a normal or changed landscape, and see the estimated HH and HV response with its uncertainty.

What we saw in Haiti (Specifically in Artibonite, Haiti)

On the 30 October pass, 5.3% of 13,860 squares (HH, threshold 3) differed from their own history, mostly in a block near the western coast and a patch in the north-east. We treat these as places to inspect, not as confirmed change. Our hypotheses are standing water, vegetation change, a large rain just before that pass, or processing differences, since our passes mix provisional and validated NISAR processing. HH tends to respond to ground and water surfaces and HV to vegetation structure, so comparing both helps separate these ideas. Field data would be needed to confirm any of them.

Benefits and intended impact

With LAND MEMORY, instead of looking at one satellite image at a time, researchers can see how a place usually behaves and where it departs from that. This can help decide where to look more closely, compare similar landscapes, and plan field visits.

Tools and technologies

Python and Flask for the server. "asf_search" and "fsspec" to find and read NISAR files, earthaccess for IMERG rainfall, xarray, rioxarray, rasterio, h5netcdf and NumPy for processing. MapLibre GL JS and Chart.js for the map and charts. Hosted on PythonAnywhere for one month free.

What makes it creative

LAND MEMORY focuses on how each place behaves over time, not just how it looks on one day. It combines radar, rainfall history, and land cover, and lets people test rainfall scenarios on the same screen where they inspect the data.

Limitations and future work

A radar anomaly does not prove flooding, a change in soil moisture, or any specific cause. NISAR calibrated data only starts in June 2026, so each square has a short history of about 11 passes. Rainfall data is about 10 km wide while squares are 250 m. The NISAR quality mask is not used yet. The Scenario Explorer (Which we call the Digital Shadow or Statistical Twin) is a simple statistical model and has not been validated. Next steps are ground validation, and adding vegetation, terrain, and soil information.

Use of AI

Parts of the code and text were debugged and developed with Claude (Anthropic).
